# Five researched running articles — 25 October 2026

These are the five topics selected in the preceding Ubersuggest research pass.
US / English estimates retrieved 25 October 2026: marathon pacer 4,400 / SD 20;
half marathon pacing 4,400 / SD 27; yasso 800s 1,300 / SD 19; carb loading
calculator 480 / SD 12; longest run before marathon 170 / SD 23. The earlier
pass screened 22 keywords and 10 SERPs. Figures are cached search estimates,
not measured site visits or forecasts. Several SERPs contain AI Overviews.
The more optimistic alternative keyword's difficulty was not used to imply an
easy ranking. No monthly-credit metrics refresh or generated article was bought.

## Research and original contribution

| Article | Reader's task and original work | Competition and overlap control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marathon pacers | Work out which timing clock applies, what different start offsets mean, and the pace required to erase a same-marker time gap. Printable questions and a catch-up worksheet. | Read Sara Kurth's experienced-pacer account, which already covers group logistics. Our contribution is worked timing arithmetic, rather than restating a definition. Links to the existing pace-band and run-walk tools. |
| Half-marathon pacing | Create cumulative 5/10/15/20 km checkpoints and compare even pacing with a slower first 5 km at a fixed finish target. Use Davin's existing recorded laps with their limitations. | Read MyProCoach's pacing guide. This article supplies editable, fully calculated checkpoints. It does not duplicate the race-comparison article or create thin goal-time variants. |
| Yasso 800s | Count all rep and recovery time, distinguish equal-time and distance recoveries, and understand the traditional digit label's limitations. | Read Run with Raj's firsthand workout description and the origin account on Bart Yasso's site. Recovery variants are identified explicitly. No pass mark, accuracy margin or marathon-readiness guarantee is invented. |
| Carb-loading calculator | Translate a selected daily target into label-based portions; distinguish planned, recorded and unknown intake; download a one-day record. | Read Featherstone Nutrition's substantial guide. Competitors already have target calculators; ours adds editable serving definitions and separate planned/recorded food accounting. No copied menu or fabricated food-composition data. |
| Longest run | Compare 24/28/30/32 km time budgets, weekly share and distance change against the prior 30 days. Analyse the existing 32 km personal account without inventing a controlled experiment. | Existing long-run article covers effort formats. This page handles distance/duration and surrounding workload. No universal three-hour limit, weekly-share rule or injury-clearance badge. |

## Claim-to-source record

Primary and official sources were checked through web retrieval/search on 25
October 2026. Some journal/PMC pages returned access challenges; accessible
publisher text, indexed original abstracts, author archives and official sources
were used instead. No bypass of a sign-in wall was attempted.

- Chicago Marathon official pace-team FAQ:
  <https://www.chicagomarathon.com/event-info/participant-information/pace-team/>
  — chip timing and corral example. Event-specific details are qualified.
- Austin Marathon official pacer page: <https://youraustinmarathon.com/pacers/>
  — useful counterexample: one group on gun time, others on chip time, with
  leader-dependent aid-station arrangements. Readers must check their edition.
- Nikolaidis, Čuk and Knechtle (2019), PMID 30646638:
  <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30646638/> — observational half-marathon
  pacing. The opening offset is original arithmetic, not a proven optimum.
- Amby Burfoot's origin account on Bart Yasso's site:
  <https://www.bartyasso.com/800s> — history and anecdotal digit comparison.
- Runner's World workout convention:
  <https://www.runnersworld.com/training/a20799355/yasso-800s/>
- Raj Hathiramani's firsthand account:
  <https://www.runwithraj.com/blog/2018/11/30/my-favorite-track-workout-yasso-800s>
  — documents a different recovery description. No collapse instruction is adopted.
- Prediction Equations for Marathon Performance (2019), PMID 31575820:
  <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31575820/> — general limits of prediction,
  not evidence validating the Yasso protocol.
- Burke et al., IAAF nutrition consensus (2019), DOI 10.1123/ijsnem.2019-0065:
  <https://journals.humankinetics.com/view/journals/ijsnem/29/2/article-p73.xml>
  and official World Athletics copy:
  <https://worldathletics.org/download/download?filename=23fb9de0-6699-4d5b-b075-42f5da5518f5.pdf&urlslug=Nutrition+for+Athletics+-+2019+IAAF+Consensus+Statement>
  — general daily loading range and duration. No individual target is prescribed.
- FDA label guidance:
  <https://www.fda.gov/food/nutrition-facts-label/how-understand-and-use-nutrition-facts-label>
  — serving versus container interpretation.
- AIS pre-exercise sports-food context:
  <https://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/nutrition/supplements/group_a/sports-foods2/sports-bar2/how-and-when-do-i-use-it>
- Fokkema et al. (2020), DOI 10.1111/sms.13725:
  <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/sms.13725>
  — distance-category associations; self-report and category-size limits retained.
- Frandsen et al. (2025), PMID 40623829:
  <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40623829/> — session-distance context. Not
  extrapolated into a safe weekly progression or personal probability.
- B.A.A. official training descriptions:
  <https://www.baa.org/races/boston-marathon/info-for-athletes/boston-marathon-training/>
  — one distance example, without reproducing a copyrighted schedule.
- Marine Corps Marathon coaching discussion:
  <https://www.marinemarathon.com/when-should-i-progress-my-mileage-by-how-much-per-week/>
  — practical time-cap context, explicitly distinguished from trial evidence.

## Experience, attribution and presentation

Davin's established biography identifies him as a recreational runner and site
creator. No new qualification, nutrition review, pacer experience, completed
workout, race result or successful food trial is claimed. Personal examples link
to the existing Run Melbourne and fueling records. Watch laps are not relabelled
official timing splits. Hypothetical nutrition labels and meal-allocation budgets
are identified as illustrations, rather than verified composition or a full diet.
The existing editorial policy explains software/AI assistance.

Each article has its own body, original examples, Article/Breadcrumb metadata,
canonical URL and 1200 × 630 typographic social card. Research links appear beside
the relevant claims and in source notes. No invented expert review or rich-result
eligibility is asserted. All five tools show the assumptions in the article and
in `/methodology/`. Forms enhance static articles; no-JavaScript readers retain
tables, formulas and examples. Food records stay in memory and can be downloaded.

Twelve existing contextual locations link into the new articles, in addition to
the blog index and HTML/XML sitemaps. The navigation baseline is extended only
with the five new URLs; all previous title/H1/description/canonical/robots
contracts remain intact. Existing calculator algorithms, consent, adverts,
affiliate destinations and redirects are not changed.

## Rebuilding and verification

Run `python .github/quality/build-researched-guides.py` for HTML and
`python .github/quality/build-researched-social-cards.py` for social cards. These
are development helpers; the site remains static with no production build.

The dedicated browser suite exercises all five worksheets, unit interpretation,
invalid-state clearing, unknown versus zero food records, CSV quoting and formula
protection, metadata, source presence, four viewport widths, WCAG axe checks,
actual printable PDFs and the no-JavaScript reading path. Broader navigation,
calculator and prior-guide regressions accompany this change. One independently
rounded half-marathon checkpoint was corrected from 1:25:28 to 1:25:29 during QA.
